_comment: Example structural gate config. Every check here is one where the check IS the thing meant - no proxy in between. Copy, edit, delete what doesn't apply. Keys beginning with underscore are ignored.
_required_sections: Headings that must exist AND have a non-empty body. Case-insensitive. Catches the silent-omission failure: the section that was supposed to be there and just isn't.
_max_words: A length cap is not a proxy for quality - if the rule is 'two pages', the rule literally is a length. Roughly 500 words per page.
_required_phrases: Text that must appear verbatim. Use for standards codes, required attributions, mandated disclaimers.
_forbidden_phrases: The rescued form of an unfalsifiable virtue. 'Be equity-aware' cannot be checked; 'these assumptions must not appear' can. Presence is objectively verifiable and gaming the check requires satisfying it.
forbidden_phrases: when you were younger, your parents
_define_before_use: Terms whose first appearance must be inside the definition section. Catches the ordering failure that a mere presence check misses - a vocabulary box at the end of the page is not scaffolding.
_companion_files: Files that must exist alongside the artifact. Answer keys are the usual case - they get forgotten, and their absence is invisible until someone needs one.
_rejected: These keys are refused by validate_artifact.py on purpose: max_grade_level, reading_level, flesch_kincaid, max_sentence_words, vocabulary_difficulty. All are proxies. Blocking on them teaches sentence-chopping, which strips connectives and can make text score easier while reading harder. Run scan_prose.py for those signals instead - advisory, located, unscored.
